description: Assemble one continuous edit from 2 camera files of the same event that started rolling at different moments. It syncs the cameras from their audio (a clap or sharp sound in the first 30 seconds of every file is the fallback), picks the camera that frames each voice by diarization, and renders one video at the main camera's resolution and fps (1080p ceiling). Three calls: (1) call with `inputs` (array of `{filename, name?}`, index 0 = the main camera) to receive {job_id, payment_challenge}. (2) After payment, call again with `job_id` (+ `payment_credential` on the MPP rail) to receive `upload_urls[]`: one presigned PUT URL per camera, 1h expiry. (3) PUT every file to its URL, call complete_upload(job_id) once ALL are uploaded (a partial upload is rejected naming the missing indices), then poll get_job_status(job_id). Optional `offsets` (seconds per camera, `offsets[0]` = 0, others may be negative) skip clap detection for footage with no clap; optional `cuts` (`{source, start, end}` in each camera's own timeline) render exactly the angles you give and skip automatic selection; `show` (`speaker` default, or `listener`) and `n_speakers` tune automatic selection. Output: role `edit`, one H.264 video with audio loudness-normalized to -14 LUFS / -1.5 dBTP, as long as the main camera and at most 60 minutes. Flat price for the whole job regardless of camera count: $3.00, see /.well-known/mpp.json for the Tempo USDC rate. Allow about 1.5 minutes of processing per minute of footage, plus upload time. The result is a normal video job: pass its `job_id` to clips_from_job as `source_job_id` to cut clips from the finished edit (it stays in storage 72h). Use for multi-camera interviews, podcasts and panels; use clips_from_job instead to cut a single existing video. Voice-based selection only (no gaze). Retrying with `job_id` alone recovers the current state or fresh upload URLs. Failed jobs auto-refund. Payment: pay by credit card via the Stripe Checkout link (open the returned `payment_url` in any browser) or Tempo USDC via mppx; the challenge's WWW-Authenticate header and /.well-known/mpp.json are authoritative for which methods are offered.
name: edit_from_multiple_cameras
